values.title: Privacy Policy
values.intro: Information on the processing of personal data of visitors to the website (petrik.hu).

values.html:
Who we are

Our website address is: ../

What personal data we collect and why we collect it

Comments

When a comment is submitted, in addition to the data entered in the comment form, the commenter's IP address and browser user agent string are collected in order to help filter out spam.

An anonymised string created from your e-mail address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service if it is in use on the site. The Gravatar service's terms can be viewed at: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After your comment is approved, the content of your comment and your profile picture become publicly visible.

Media

If a registered user uploads images to the website, images containing embedded location data (EXIF GPS) should be avoided. Visitors to the website can download and extract location data from images on the website.

Contact forms

Cookies

If you leave a comment on the website, your name, e-mail address and website address are saved in cookies. This is for your convenience, so that you do not have to fill in these fields again when you write another comment. These cookies last for one year.

If you visit the login page, we set a temporary cookie to determine whether your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal information and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in to the website, we set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display options. Login cookies last for two days, and the cookie storing screen display options lasts for one year. If you select “Remember me”, your login will persist for two weeks. When you log out, the login cookies are removed.

If you edit or publish a post or page, an additional cookie is saved in your browser. This cookie contains no personal data; it simply stores the ID of the post you edited. It expires after one day.

Embedded content from other websites

Posts on the website may include embedded content from external sources (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from external sources behaves in exactly the same way as if the visitor had visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies or third-party tracking code, and monitor your interaction with the embedded content, including tracking your interaction if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Analytics

Who we share your data with

How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so that any subsequent comments can be recognised and approved automatically, instead of being held in the moderation queue.

For users who register on the website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit or delete their personal information at any time (except that they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

If you have a registered account on this website or have left comments, you can request an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal or security purposes.

Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

values.title: For more than 140 years, value has been the measure.
values.intro: The school opened on 7 December 1879 under the name State Industrial Secondary School – and since then it has been one of the oldest and most respected institutions of Hungarian vocational training.

values.title: Petrik Lajos
values.html: The school's namesake, Lajos Petrik, was a teacher at the institution from 1880 and its director from 1905 to 1914. His career was characterised by openness to the challenges of science, the fine arts and nature. He was at once a scientist, teacher, ceramist, art collector and nature lover.

rows.text: On 7 December the State Industrial Secondary School opens its doors, with mechanical engineering, architecture and chemistry specialisations. Its first building stood at 4 Főherceg Sándor (today Gutenberg) Square.
The school moves into the new building complex designed by Alajos Hauszmann (at the corner of József körút and Népszínház utca). Its director is Károly Hegedűs, who led the institution for 35 years.
Its new name is Royal Hungarian State Higher Industrial School; four main specialisations: mechanical engineering, chemical industry, metal and iron industry, woodworking industry.
The chemical industry specialisation moves to the building at Thököly út 48, which is still the school's home today.

Alongside the traditional chemical industry training, IT and environmental protection training grows up. In 2007/2008, merging with the Irinyi János Secondary School of Environmental Protection and Chemical Industry, Petrik becomes the largest environmental protection and chemical industry training institution in the country.
From 1 July the school's maintainer is the Budapest Technical Vocational Training Centre.
The 140th anniversary of the founding of the school. In the HVG “Secondary School 2019” publication, it ranks 10th nationwide among vocational secondary schools.

items.title: Our creed and goals
items.html:
The versatility represented by our namesake, Lajos Petrik, and the acceptance and passing on of values are the goals on which our school's past, present and future are built. Our aim is to run a student-centred and, through that, partner-oriented school. Our school is open to social expectations and changing labour market needs, strives to meet these tasks through continuous innovation and renewal, and cooperates mutually with its professional partners.

In our teaching and educational work, we take into account and build into our programme the needs of parents, students and employers. In the modern, well-equipped classrooms, laboratories, IT workshops and industrial modelling workshops located in the school's two buildings, students can acquire the theoretical and practical knowledge of their trades.

items.title: Our famous former students
items.html: Our school has always taken great care to develop its students' abilities as broadly as possible and, alongside its recognised high-standard vocational training, to provide a higher level of general education. Among our former students we are proud to count, among others, the world-famous writer Nádas Péter, the philosopher Vajda Mihály, one of the founders of the Budapest School, Kovács László, former foreign minister and European Union commissioner, as well as outstanding figures of Hungarian classical and popular music such as Oberfrank Géza, former conductor of the Opera House, Demjén Ferenc, Korda György and Földes László (Hobo).

items.title: International relations
items.html: We pay special attention to nurturing international relations and take part continuously in the Erasmus+ programme. We currently have partner schools and partner institutions in Denmark, Portugal, Poland, Croatia, Spain, Greece, Lithuania, Italy and Cyprus.

items.title: Recognition and maintainer
items.html:
In the HVG publication “Secondary School 2019”, our school achieved 10th place nationwide in the ranking of vocational secondary schools. According to the publication, “The vocational secondary schools at the top of the ranking belong to the elite of vocational training […]”.

Our school's maintainer since 1 July 2015 has been the Budapest Technical Vocational Training Centre.

values.title: IT and Telecommunications
values.intro: Programming, Networking, Electronics, 3D Printing, Robotics and much more.

values.html: We recommend the IT technician programme to you if

items.title: you want to develop your 21st-century skills,
you want to strengthen your digital literacy,
you are looking for a programme that builds a bridge to the future and gives you a competitive profession,
you would like to take part in project-based education not only within lessons but also in national and international programmes,
you would like to test your knowledge, both individually and in teams, in exciting themed weeks,
you are open to challenges,
you would like to learn in an environment where we model the real world and solve problems taken from real life,
you would like to learn to think at the systems level.

values.html:
At the technical school, alongside the subjects that prepare you for the school-leaving exam, you also study vocational subjects. As part of this, in the first two years of the programme you take part in the sectoral basic education in IT and telecommunications, at the end of which you sit the sectoral basic exam. From the eleventh grade onwards you study the vocational subjects of the Software Developer and Tester or the IT Systems and Applications Operator technician qualification. You will become familiar with the basics of programming and networking, the network devices of large companies, software testing, mobile programming and the operation of cloud services.

Within the technician programme, two vocational specialisations can be chosen at our school.

values.title: 5 0613 12 03 – Software Developer and Tester
values.html:
This is the profession for you if you are interested in how the applications we use every day come to life, whether on a desktop computer or on mobile.

After completing your technician studies, you can find work at IT companies as a programmer or software tester, or you can continue your studies in higher education, but already with solid foundations.

5 0612 12 02 – IT Systems and Applications Operator Technician

This is the profession for you if you are interested in how the networks of small and large companies are built and what their maintenance and operation involve, and in how companies make use of the opportunities offered by cloud services.

Once you have completed the programme, you can take up work at companies as an IT system administrator or network operator, or you can continue your studies in higher education, but already with solid foundations.

Vocational qualifications and add-on qualifications

values.title: 06135002 – Mobile Application Developer
values.html: Smartphones and tablets are now among the most widely used IT devices, so native applications built for mobile platforms are of outstanding importance. A mobile application developer is a software developer with at least technician-level knowledge and skills who is able to develop native Android or iOS-based mobile applications. They independently carry out the complete implementation of a simple or moderately complex mobile application, and in a team they develop individual components of more complex mobile applications. They know one of the programming languages needed for mobile development (Kotlin, Java or Swift). They confidently know and use at least one platform suitable for iOS or Android-based mobile application development (Android Studio, XCode, etc.). They are familiar with the basic principles of mobile application development. By using the typical controls and structural elements used on mobile platforms, they create a user interface that provides an optimal appearance on different screen sizes and pixel densities alike. Where necessary, they use multimedia components to develop components capable of playing video and audio. In RESTful architecture systems, they implement REST API client functionality within the mobile application. They manage data using local data storage, an external database connection or BaaS (Backend-as-a-Service). They solve problems arising in their work independently by web searching and using online knowledge bases. They are open to applying new technologies and continuously develop their knowledge. They communicate effectively in both Hungarian and English on professional topics.

values.title: 06135001 – Web Developer
values.html:
The vast majority of software being created today runs in a web environment, so no programmer or software developer can do without knowledge of web technologies. A web developer is a software developer with at least technician-level knowledge and skills who, in addition to general programming knowledge, is able to develop applications that run in a web environment. They are able to independently carry out the complete implementation of a simple or moderately complex web application, including building the server-side component (backend), programming the client-side component (frontend), and designing the related database schema. In a team, they independently implement the backend or frontend components of more complex web systems, or sub-components thereof. To carry out the above tasks, they have confident, up-to-date knowledge and practical skills in the most important web technologies. They create standard web pages in the HTML5 markup language and style web pages using CSS3 stylesheets. They program dynamic web pages in JavaScript. They build client-side applications using a JavaScript framework (e.g. React, Vue, Angular). They build server-side applications using a suitable language or framework (e.g. Node.js, PHP, Laravel, Spring, etc.). They solve problems arising in their work independently by web searching and using online knowledge bases. They are open to applying new technologies and continuously develop their knowledge. They communicate effectively in both Hungarian and English on professional topics.

values.html: We recommend the environmental protection technician programme to you if

items.title: you like being outdoors and being active,

you would like to take an active part in preserving our environment.

values.html:
You can become an environmental protection technician after five years of technical school education. At the technical school, alongside the subjects that prepare you for the school-leaving exam, you also study vocational subjects. As part of this, in the first two years of the programme you take part in the sectoral basic education in environmental protection and water management, at the end of which you sit the sectoral basic exam. From the eleventh grade onwards you study the vocational subjects of the environmental protection technician qualification. You will become familiar with the basics of environmental protection, the equipment used to protect the environment, and the field and laboratory tests that examine the state of the environment.

In the environmental protection technician programme, you can choose from the following specialisations.

values.title: Environmental Protection Specialisation
values.html: We recommend it to those who like working in a laboratory and are precise and thorough, who are able to concentrate on a single task for a long time, but who are also happy to leave the laboratory to take environmental samples.

values.title: Nature Conservation Specialisation
values.html: We recommend it to those who are dedicated to preserving nature, who gladly spend a significant part of their time outdoors tending and managing natural habitats and examining living organisms. They are not afraid of the physical work involved in nature conservation, nor of keeping computer records.

Administration
specialisation

We recommend it to those who like administrative tasks and take the protection of our environment to heart. We recommend it to those who like writing and reading and gladly use a computer for all of this. They also enjoy talking and communicating with others. Handling environmental data requires great attention, so we recommend this field primarily to those who are orderly and precise.

values.title: Waste Recovery and Processing Specialisation
values.html:
We recommend it to those who like carrying out measurements and tests. We recommend it to those who are interested in how a machine works and are happy to set up or operate waste management machines and equipment. We also recommend it to those who are thorough and pay attention to every detail, and so can easily follow the operation of a complex system.

values.title: Community Service
values.intro: Social and environmental activity serving the good of the student’s local community

values.html:
Dear Students!

Would you like to create something new together with your classmates? Do you also want to do something for others? Would you like to take part in a community project in which you can help children, people in need and animals together with your friends, while also completing your compulsory community service?

Through community service you can not only solve a problem, but also learn, almost without noticing, about cooperation, conflict management, empathy, creative thinking, project planning, decision-making and taking responsibility. You can make use of these newly acquired competences later when looking for work.

In the current special situation, schools may also involve students in the school process of digital education outside the classroom, so you can help and mentor your fellow students online.

After 1 January 2016, the condition for issuing the school-leaving exam certificate is proof of completing 50 hours of “community service”.

“Community service: an individual or group activity that is social, environmental or serves the good of the student’s local community, carried out within an organised framework, independent of financial interest, and its pedagogical processing.”

Legal background of School Community Service

Act CXC of 2011 on National Public Education, Hungarian Gazette No. 162, 29 December 2011

In the related implementing decree, the provisions on community service are as follows:

  • At the site of the community service, assisting the person concerned by the service may be carried out on school days in a time frame of at least one and at most three hours per occasion, and outside school days in a time frame of at least one and at most five hours per occasion.
  • For the purposes of completing community service, one hour means sixty minutes of community service time, with the proviso that the time of travelling to the site and travelling home from the site cannot be counted towards completion.
  • The teacher coordinating the community service for the given student holds, within the fifty hours – together with the mentor where necessary – a preparatory session of up to five hours and then a closing session of up to five hours. (EMMI Decree 20/2012 (VIII. 31.))

Relevant acts and decrees

  • Act LXXX of 2019 on vocational training, Government Decree 12/2020 (II. 7.) on the implementation of the Act on vocational training
  • Government Decree 100/1997 (VI. 13.) on the issuing of the exam regulations for the school-leaving exam
  • Government Decree 12/2020 (II. 7.) on the implementation of the Act on vocational training, §107, §258.

Further professional recommendations

  • Act LXXXVIII of 2005 on voluntary activity in the public interest
  • Government Decree 110/2012 (VI. 4.) on the issuing, introduction and application of the National Core Curriculum
  • National Volunteer Strategy 2011-2020
  • Civil law: Act CLXXV of 2011 on the right of association, public benefit status, and the operation and support of civil organisations

You can read more about School Community Service here

  • http://kozossegi.ofi.hu/
  • https://i-dia.org/korabbi-projektek/iskolai-kozossegi-szolgalat-x/

IKSZ – Basic Principles

items.title: Strengthening the local community:
items.html: A task carried out during community service means an activity or activities that serve the good of the local community and that take place at the school or in its immediate surroundings, possibly within a radius of a few kilometres, or at the student’s place of residence or its immediate surroundings.

items.title: Principle of free choice:
items.html: In consultation with parents and teachers, students may choose the activities they will carry out from among those organised by the school or proposed by themselves and accepted by the school.

items.title: Principle of independence from financial interest:
items.html: In connection with school community service, no financial interest of the parties (teacher, institution, host organisation, private individual, student, parent) may arise in the programme, and the students’ activity may not bring anyone any advantage or profit of this kind.

items.title: Principle of an organised framework:
items.html: It is the task and responsibility of the secondary school to organise and coordinate school community service, therefore it is required that creditable activities may only be carried out as organised by the school. Before starting the activity, the student must have the approval of the authorised school person, the person responsible for the task, and their parents.

items.title: Principle of dual purpose:
items.html: The activities must combine the nature of service with experiential, pedagogy-based learning. Carrying out community service also requires the presence of a learning process.

items.title: Principle of reciprocity:
items.html: The helper and the person in need of help are actively involved in the programme to the extent of their abilities. During preparation, students must be made sensitive to the experience of reciprocity, so that they are open and accepting towards the person they come into contact with.

items.title: Principle of directness:
items.html: In community service, the activity must serve not the organisation itself but directly the organisation's target group. Interpersonal cooperation and partnership develop between the helper (student) and the person in need of help, which places the emphasis on genuine relationships between people and is suitable for shaping personality and developing self-knowledge.

items.title: Principle of cooperation:
items.html: In connection with community service, a partnership develops among all those involved at the school or the host organisation; no hierarchy may appear in the relationship between teacher and student, host organisation and student, or the person cared for or helped and the student.

items.title: Principle of proportionality:
items.html: A student may complete the IKSZ (school community service) only partly at a school body (e.g. the student council) or at an external organisation of which they are a member. Tasks of this kind that are performed anyway (e.g. involving the student council, a sports club, a choir or any other organisation) do not in themselves count as community service. If the activity is supplemented with an active, individual extra task performed in the areas of school community service mentioned in the legislation, it can be credited, in a proportion accepted by the school, as part of the required 50 hours.

items.title: Principle of variety:
items.html: From the point of view of the basic pedagogical aim, it is important that the student completes the so-called contact hours (min. 40 hours) in several areas (e.g. three), based on regularly recurring activities.

items.title: Principle of sustainability:
items.html: Students should, wherever possible, take part in activities that are sustainable in the long term and are also beneficial for later year groups and for those being helped.

items.title: Principle of impartiality:
items.html: A student may not perform community service for a close relative or at that relative's direct workplace. Visiting grandparents, relatives in need of help or close family members is valuable in itself, but it cannot be credited as part of the IKSZ.

values.html:
Source: www.kozossegi.ofi.hu

What you need to do about school community service – IKSZ timeline

items.title: I. Application
items.html: At the beginning of the year, fill in the application form found on the school website and hand it in to your form teacher.

items.title: II. Finding host organisations
items.html:
Think about which areas you would most like to try yourself in and where you would most like to help! You can also look for a host organisation yourself, one that welcomes you gladly and is close to your home or the school. If you do not know where to start, come and we will help you.

The school has cooperation agreements with the following continuously expanding list of institutions

items.title: III. Cooperation
items.html: Once you have found the place that suits you, where you would gladly volunteer, find a mentor who will help you with carrying out the tasks within the organisation. In the case of a healthcare, social or charity organisation, you will find the cooperation agreement template on the website; fill it in, have it signed, and hand it in, in 2 copies, to the IKSZ coordinator.

items.title: IV. IKSZ log
items.html: During school time, a maximum of 3 hours after lessons may be entered in the log for a day; at weekends and during school breaks, a maximum of 5 hours at any time of day. Keep your hours, experiences and observations in chronological order, and show them to your form teacher every semester so that they can record the completed hours in the e-log.

items.title: V. Report
items.html: Document your activity, take photos, write reports. Share your experiences and observations with your form teacher and your class, either in a personal conversation or in writing.

items.title: VI. Completion
items.html: Hooray, you have your 50 hours! Hand your log in to your form teacher so that they can close it and enter it in the appropriate documents. They will then pass it on to the IKSZ coordinator, who issues the certificate required to start the school-leaving exams.

values.html:
Questions and misconceptions

Regarding activity documentation

items.title: May students perform work within the framework of community service?
items.html: NO – Community service may not be aimed at performing job duties defined at the institution, and none of the parties (student, host institution, client, school, etc.) may gain financial benefit from the student's activity.

items.title: Can voluntary activities done before secondary school be credited as community service?
items.html: NO – School community service can only be completed during years 9–12 of secondary school.

items.title: Is it the task of students and parents to look for host places and organise activities?
items.html: NO – Organising and coordinating school community service is the task and responsibility of the secondary school; creditable activities can only be performed when organised by the school. Before starting the activity, the student must have the approval of the authorised school person, the person responsible for the task and (on the application form) their parents. At the same time, of course, students and parents may also suggest host institutions to the school and help build partner relationships.

items.title: Is it mandatory to conclude a cooperation agreement with every host institution?
items.html: NO – Although the legislation does not in every case make concluding a cooperation agreement mandatory, it is worth setting out the framework of the activity in writing; this serves the interests of everyone involved.

items.title: Must the host institution issue a separate certificate of the students' activity every time?
items.html:
NOT MANDATORY – In the programme, the host institutions are the schools' partners, and the tasks tailored to them and expected of them are based on an agreement between the two parties (school and host institution). There is no mandatory element of administration concerning students on the part of the host institutions, but it is in any case advisable to think all this through – to protect those involved, and in line with the rationality of everyday practice. An attendance sheet is a relatively simple document, and it can prevent
later misunderstandings.

items.title: Does the school keep the students' community service log?
items.html: NO – The student log is a tool that helps track activities and supports pedagogical guidance and reflection. It follows from this function that it can only achieve its real purpose if it is kept by the students.

values.html: Host organisations

items.title: Can only an organisation listed in the Community Service Portal database be a host institution?
items.html: NO – A host institution need not be one listed in the Portal database; the school may freely approach its partners. The Portal is a good opportunity for those involved to find one another.

items.title: Can community service also be completed with grandparents, relatives or at parents' workplaces?
items.html: THIS IS NOT QUITE TRUE – A student may not perform community service for a close relative or at that relative's direct workplace. Visiting grandparents, relatives in need of help or close family members is valuable in itself, but it cannot be credited as part of the IKSZ. Students may perform community service at their parents' workplace if their activity is not under the mentoring or supervision of their own parents.

items.title: May students perform community service only within a 30 km radius of the school or their place of residence?
items.html: NO – There is no legislation concerning the place of completion linked to a 30 km radius of the school or place of residence. The sustainability of the programme and safe access to the location may be considerations when selecting host organisations.

items.title: Can community service also be completed at companies and businesses?
items.html: NO – Community service can be performed at state, municipal, civil or non-profit organisations, at a private individual on the basis of an agreement between the secondary school and the private individual, at the school's own institution, and even at a place of residence. Ensuring legal compliance in this respect is the school's task.

items.title: Must the fifty hours of community service be completed at at least three different organisations?
items.html: NO – This is not an element required by law, but in line with the intention behind the programme and for the more effective achievement of the pedagogical goals, it is recommended to carry out activities in several different areas. When determining the total number of hours spent on individual activities, it is worth taking into account the characteristics of the individual organisations and areas of activity.

items.title: Can community service be done in one's own school?
items.html: YES – It can also be done at one's own institution, provided the activities comply with the legal requirements and the basic principles.

items.title: Can community service be done at private individuals?
items.html: YES – On the basis of the secondary school's agreement, community service can also be done at a private individual, provided it complies with the requirements and the activity done this way and the circumstances of its completion can be mapped out in advance.

values.html: Scheduling

items.title: Must a rest day be observed between two consecutive occasions of the activities?
items.html: NO – Students may do community service for at least one and at most three hours per occasion, regardless of whether it is a school day or not.

items.title: Can community service not be done at weekends, during school breaks or in summer?
items.html: THIS IS NOT QUITE TRUE – It is within the school's competence to decide whether it undertakes running community service activities falling on non-school days, since for these occasions it must provide a school coordinator who is reachable at least by telephone.

items.title: Is it enough to complete the 50 hours of community service by the day the school-leaving certificate is issued?
items.html: NO – In the school-leaving exam period immediately following the completion of secondary school, the condition for starting the school-leaving exams is certification of completing fifty hours of community service.

values.html:
Points to consider when preparing the closing report on community service

We ask students to also answer the following questions in their report (the order of the questions need not be followed)

  • Of the community service opportunities offered by the school, why did you choose precisely this area/these areas or organisations?
  • Before starting community service, did you take part in a preparatory/sensitising session, and if so, what kind was it?
  • Describe the specific activity you carried out! If possible, illustrate your report with photos, video, etc.
  • What expectations did you have when you began the service?
  • What positive, or perhaps negative, experiences did you have while completing the service?
  • How do you see it: have you changed in any way while completing community service? If so, in what way?
  • In your opinion, what knowledge did community service give you? Did certain skills and abilities develop, e.g. sense of responsibility, independence, empathy, etc.?
  • Have you become more sensitive to the problems of the world around you?
  • Does community service influence your choice of career?
  • What would you advise fellow students who have not yet started the service?

items.title: LanguageCert state-recognised international English language exam
items.html:
The LanguageCert exams are the successors of the City & Guilds English language exams, after the English company Peoplecert Qualifications acquired the intellectual property rights of the City & Guilds exams and ensures the international continuity of the exams.

The LanguageCert International English Language Exams are an English language exam system listed in one of the United Kingdom's official reference frameworks, and are accepted in several European countries.

Peoplecert is a global organisation engaged in exam development and exam administration, which over the past nearly 20 years has built its reputation in more than 150 countries around the world by developing information technology and management exams and by designing and operating online examination platforms.

The exam, designed for the 6 levels of the Common European Framework of Reference, offers numerous advantages for university admission, degrees, studies at home and abroad, and employment. Its structure aims for simplicity and measures general, communicative English language proficiency with everyday, real-life tasks.

The use of a monolingual dictionary is permitted during the exam. The LanguageCert exam centre supports exam preparation with up-to-date teaching materials, downloadable sample tasks, assessed mock exams and preparatory exercises.

The exam consists of reading, writing, speaking and listening parts. The language exam can only be taken at accredited exam venues, either as a complex exam or separately as a written or oral partial exam. In addition to the international certificate, candidates also receive a state-recognised language exam certificate for successfully passed written and oral partial exams.

items.title: Advantages of the language exam
items.html:
• internationally recognised monolingual language exam
  • emphasises practical, communicative language skills
  • the tasks are everyday and true to life
  • the use of a monolingual dictionary is permitted during the exam
  • the oral exam takes the form of a teacher–student dialogue, with no on-the-spot assessment

items.title: Assessment of the language exam

The final result of the complex exam is made up of the results of the written and oral parts: if the candidate achieves at least a PASS result in both parts, the LanguageCert complex language exam is successful.

For a successful written partial exam, candidates must achieve at least a PASS result in the assessment of reading (Reading) and writing (Writing).

For a successful oral partial exam, candidates must achieve a minimum of a PASS result in the assessment of listening (Listening) and speaking (Speaking).

items.html:
Central written exam for all programmes: mathematics and Hungarian language. For students with dysfunctional disorders, we provide extra time on a request supported by an expert opinion.

items.title: Assessment of the candidate's performance
items.html:
It is based on the academic points brought from primary school and the results achieved in the entrance exam.

Brought results: the end-of-year grades of year 7 and the mid-year grades of year 8 in Hungarian language and literature, history, foreign language, mathematics, physics, chemistry, geography, biology and IT. A grade of excellent (5) is worth 2 points, good (4) 1 point; unsatisfactory, pass and satisfactory (1–3) are worth 0 points. If the grade is excellent in all 10 subjects in each of the two terms, a maximum of 40 points can be obtained in total.

values.title: Post-matura technician programmes
values.intro: Our post-matura technician programmes

values.html:
We recommend our post-matura technician programmes to students who:

  • are not yet sure whether they will continue at university or college, but definitely want to acquire marketable professional skills;
  • want to lay the foundations of their professional knowledge for further specialised study;
  • want to acquire, within 2 years, a profession offering high starting salaries;
  • would like to work in a profession where continuous further training is available;
  • wish to receive, in the full-time programme, a state-guaranteed scholarship that can be equal to the minimum wage during their studies;
  • would like to start working alongside their studies – for them we recommend our evening programmes;
  • are interested in practice-oriented training.

BMSZC Petrik Lajos Bilingual Technical School, one of the oldest and most highly regarded technical schools in the country, offers all of this to those interested in our technician programmes.

Our school is located not far from the city centre, on the routes of buses 5, 7, 7E, 8E, 30, 30A, 110, 112, 230 and 133E. Keleti railway station and Zugló railway station are also 7–10 minutes from the school, so it is easy to reach from the agglomeration as well, with 1 change or a 10-minute walk.

Our practical, knowledge-based programme is a guarantee that you can become a future environmental protection professional.

values.title: Chemical Industry
values.intro: Experiments, sampling, measurement, calculations and much, much more.

values.html: We recommend the chemical technician programme to you if

items.title: you are interested in chemistry and laboratory or chemical industry work,
you want to become a professional capable of solving problems,
you would like to learn the basics in well-equipped school specialist laboratories,
you would like to solve digital-minded, project-based tasks,
you would like to connect your knowledge to practice, even in a real working environment,
in the bilingual programme, you would like to hold your own in an English-speaking or international environment with your professional language competence.

values.html:
At the technical school, alongside preparing for the matura, you also study vocational subjects. In the first two years there is a chemical industry foundation: through laboratory work and theory lessons, students become familiar with the basics of the chemical industry. This stage ends with the sectoral basic exam. In 11th grade the targeted chemical technician training begins: in the form of specific practical work and vocational theory, you study organic and inorganic chemistry, general chemistry, analytics and biotechnology.

During the chemical technician programme at our school, you can choose between two vocational specialisations.

values.title: 5 0711 24 08 – General laboratory technician
values.html:
This is the profession for you if your main area of interest is laboratory work: you would take samples, prepare them and carry out measurements, or would gladly produce chemical substances.

After completing your technician studies, you will be able to find work in chemical industry plant, quality control, quality assurance and research laboratories, or, if you continue in a related field, you can use your acquired knowledge in your higher education studies.

values.title: 5 0711 24 08 – Production process controller
values.html:
This is the profession for you if you are interested in running large-scale plants: you would carry out, direct and monitor industrial processes or operate devices and equipment.

After completing your technician studies, you can find work as a technician or engineering assistant in pharmaceutical or chemical manufacturing or the petroleum industry, or, if you continue in a related field, you can use your acquired knowledge in your higher education studies.

Vocational qualifications and add-on programmes

values.title: 07115002 – Instrumental analyst qualification
values.html:
Professional prerequisite: chemical technician qualification

The instrumental analyst, working independently or under the direction of a more highly qualified professional, carries out instrumental analytical tests related to chemical, pharmaceutical, food, petroleum and environmental protection processes in research, testing or plant laboratories. They apply modern instrumental analytical methods with an IT background, using control and data-processing software. They take part in the validation of methods and processes, in the development of new analytical methods, and in external and internal audits. They carry out the sampling and sample preparation activities related to the tests. They are responsible for keeping the instruments in working order and maintaining them. They carry out their work in compliance with economic principles, quality assurance, fire safety, occupational safety, environmental protection and other relevant regulations. They document the administrative tasks related to their job in accordance with quality requirements, using the IT background.

Conditions required for organising the qualification exam and a detailed description of the exam activities of the qualification exam:

Written exam: Instrumental analytical knowledge (30%)

Project task: Preparing and presenting a portfolio (70%)

In the portfolio, the candidate presents their activities to date, their vision of the future related to the profession, and the learning outcomes achieved in the electroanalytical, spectrometric and chromatographic instrumental analytical practicals during the study of the instrumental analyst profession, including a reflection on their own learning outcomes and work activity.

Mandatory elements of the portfolio:

  • Introduction of the candidate
  • Presentation of instrumental analytical areas: presentation of laboratory tests from two freely chosen analytical areas.
  • Preparation of a final paper on one freely chosen analytical area.
  • Reflection

values.title: 07115003 – Pharmaceutical industry specialist technician qualification
values.html:
Professional prerequisite: chemical technician qualification

The pharmaceutical industry specialist technician, working independently or under the direction of a pharmacist, chemist or chemical engineer, takes part in the production of medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients. They can carry out fermentation processes. They take part in the partial or full management of pharmaceutical manufacturing processes, and in the operation and cleaning of devices and equipment. They contribute to the scale-up of manufacturing technologies and to pilot production. They can operate drug dispensing and packaging machines. They carry out quality control tests, check the quality and chemical composition of in-process and finished products, and test dosage forms based on standards and regulations. They carry out instrumental analytical and other instrumental tests. They take part in special pharmaceutical and laboratory tests and microbiological tests. They carry out chemical syntheses in the laboratory. They take part in equipment qualification and process validation. They take part in research processes and drug development and in their documentation, primarily using an IT background, and continuously train themselves further for this work. They carry out their work in compliance with economic principles and technological, hygiene, quality assurance, fire safety, occupational safety, environmental protection and other relevant regulations. They document the administrative tasks related to their job in accordance with quality requirements, using the IT background.

Conditions required for organising the qualification exam and a detailed description of the exam activities of the qualification exam:

Written exam: : Pharmaceutical industry knowledge (30%)

Project task: Pharmaceutical industry practice (70%)

The project task consists of a practical exam task and an oral interview. The candidate completes the practical task during the exam and, after finishing it, defends it orally by answering questions related to the task.

values.title: 07115003 – Drug and toxicology specialist technician
values.html:
Professional prerequisite: chemical technician qualification

The drug and toxicology specialist technician, working independently or under the direction of a person with a higher qualification, takes part in the processing of medicinal plants and carries out micro- and macromorphological examinations and quantitative and qualitative analyses related to medicinal plants and drugs. They grade medicinal plants and drugs based on the requirements of the pharmacopoeia and Hungarian and foreign standards. They take part in pharmacognostic and toxicological research. They carry out toxicological analysis of samples of various origins and perform toxicity tests. For their work they prepare the necessary chemicals, materials, tools and instruments, and use and operate them independently. They use modern IT systems and, in their work, observe the relevant hygiene, occupational safety, fire safety, environmental protection and safety regulations. They document their work accurately.

Conditions required for organising the qualification exam and a detailed description of the exam activities of the qualification exam:

Written exam: Pharmacognostic and toxicological knowledge (30%)

Project task: Pharmacognostic and toxicological practice (70%)

The project task consists of a practical exam task and an oral interview. The candidate completes the practical task during the exam, the practical exam task.
